records.name: Student Planning Association (SPA)
records.summary: The student group for City Planning students at Penn's Stuart Weitzman School of Design. It speaks up for students inside the department and school through class representatives their classmates elect, and it plans social events away from class.
records.what_you_do: Bring a student concern to the group's elected class representatives, or come to one of its social events. Past events it lists include bowling nights, pizza parties, a tailgate and a T-shirt fundraiser, but the page does not say how to join.

cost.text: Dues are not stated on the group's page.

first_step.how: Email the group to ask how to join and whether its social events are open to people outside the department.
first_step.basis: The group's page describes a student group elected by class and gives no steps for joining, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The page describes class representatives and social events, not a regular meeting, and it does not say how long events last or who attends. Ask the group before you plan to go.
first_visit_tips: Check first whether an event is for students only.
The Weitzman School is at 102 Meyerson Hall, 210 South 34th Street.

records.notes: Audience changed from public to students. The group's own page describes itself as a student group for City Planning students and does not say its events are open to the public; the tier 1 basis said they are, so please check before publishing. The page's visible contact is PennDesignSPA@gmail.com, but its mailto link text is garbled, so the Penn clubs address is kept until someone confirms which one is live. The events page lists past examples with no dates. The /spa page returned 404 and was not used.

records.name: Sub & Surface Club (Toastmasters club 00002886)
records.summary: A Toastmasters club that meets at lunchtime at the Navy Yard in South Philadelphia, in person or online, to practice public speaking. Guests are welcome, and the first meeting is free.
records.what_you_do: Practice short speeches at lunchtime meetings, and take meeting roles such as timer or evaluator.

schedule.text: Meets on the 2nd and 4th Wednesdays, noon to 1 pm, in person at the Navy Yard or online by Google Meet.

locations.label: The Navy Yard, entrance at the leasing office reached from Chapel Way

cost.text: The first meeting is free. Membership dues are not stated on the club's pages.

first_step.how: Use the club's contact form to say you want to visit, then come to a noon meeting at the Navy Yard or join online by Google Meet.
first_step.basis: The club's pages say guests are welcome at any meeting, the first meeting is free, and the club has a contact form for visitors.
first_step.what_to_expect: A meeting runs from noon to 1 pm. Guests are welcome to sit in and see how the club works, and the first meeting is free. Members practice speeches and take meeting roles.
first_visit_tips: Confirm the next meeting first, since the club's site says no upcoming meeting date has been posted.
Enter through the leasing office, reached from Chapel Way between Constitution Avenue and Normandy Place.
The club's pages do not list parking or transit, so ask through the contact form before you come.
To join online, the directions page points you to the club's email address for help.

records.notes: Schedule is from the club's home page. The meetings page says the next meeting date is still to be announced, so confirm before a visit. The contact page lists an automated Toastmasters address that says not to write to it, so it is not recorded. The phone number is carried over from tier 1 (Toastmasters listing) and is not on the club's own pages. Parking, transit and accessibility are not stated on the club's pages. Cost level changed from free to unknown: the club says the first meeting is free, but dues are not stated.

records.name: Summer-Winter Community Garden
records.summary: A volunteer-run community garden in Powelton Village, near Drexel, where members grow food on their own plots and share the work of the common areas. The garden calls itself one of the oldest community gardens in Philadelphia.
records.what_you_do: Grow food on your own plot, keep the plot and the paths beside it weeded, and attend three 3-hour Garden Days a year.

schedule.text: Garden Days are work days that typically happen at least once a month in the growing season. Each plot holder attends three 3-hour Garden Days a year.

cost.text: Dues and fees are not stated on the garden's pages.

first_step.how: Email the garden to ask for an application. Plots are given out first-come, first-served.
first_step.basis: A plot starts with an emailed application, and the pages give no waitlist, open dates or fee, so you cannot see the process before you apply.
first_step.what_to_expect: Plot holders get their own plot to grow what they like, and the gardens are mostly organic. Expect at least 2 to 3 hours a week in the growing season, plus three 3-hour Garden Days a year. The garden's pages do not state dues or fees.
first_visit_tips: Email for an application before you visit, since plots go first-come, first-served.
Plan on 2 to 3 hours a week in the growing season, plus three 3-hour Garden Days a year.
Plots must be planted by May 15 and ready for winter by the second week of December.

records.notes: No waitlist, open days, dues or accessibility are stated on the garden's pages. Work day dates are not published; members are told by email. The bylaws are referenced but not read. The four addresses are carried over from tier 1 (Neighborhood Gardens Trust listing); the garden's own pages give no street address in the text. Neighborhood Gardens Trust and PHS City Harvest are named on the garden's site and are listed in leads_only.

records.name: Summit Presbyterian Church
records.summary: A Presbyterian church on Greene Street with 10 am Sunday worship in person or on Zoom. It runs Elder Diner, a home-cooked lunch for people 55 and older, and collects supplies for blessing bags for people experiencing homelessness.
records.what_you_do: Come to Sunday worship, eat at Elder Diner (for people 55 and older), bring a main dish, salad, dessert or bread for it, drop off items for blessing bags on Sundays, or join the justice and environment committee on Zoom.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 10 am, in person or on Zoom. Elder Diner is on the first and third Tuesdays at noon, for people 55 and older. The justice and environment committee meets on the first Tuesday at 7 pm on Zoom.

cost.text: Cost is not stated on the church's site.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 10 am, in person or on Zoom, or contact the pastor to ask how to come to Elder Diner.
first_step.basis: The site invites visitors to come and see, names a pastor to contact, and gives regular times for worship and the meal.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday worship starts at 10 am and is offered in person or on Zoom. Elder Diner is a home-cooked meal and time together for adults 55 and older, at noon on the first and third Tuesdays. The site does not describe a welcome step beyond contacting the pastor.
first_visit_tips: Contact the pastor before a first Elder Diner visit to ask how it works.
Worship is also offered on Zoom if you would rather attend from home.
Blessing bag items are collected on Sundays, before and after the 10 am service.
Parking and transit are not stated on the site, so ask the church before you come.

records.notes: Accessibility (wheelchair access, elevator, hearing support) is not stated, so no access fields were written. Parking and transit are not stated. The blessing bag drop-off location is not stated. The contact page names a building administrator; not recorded. A What to Expect page is linked but was not read. The Outreach Center of Mental Health Partnerships is named as the blessing bag partner and is listed in leads_only.

records.name: Caregiver Support Group: Navigating Neurodiversity (Virtual)
records.summary: An online peer group for caregivers of neurodivergent children, listed by Healthy Minds Philly. It meets on Zoom in the evening, and you register ahead to get the meeting link.
records.what_you_do: Talk with other caregivers about the day to day side of raising a neurodivergent child, and share what has worked.

schedule.text: Held online on Zoom, 8 to 9 pm Eastern. The listing does not say how often the group meets.

cost.text: Cost is not stated on the listing.

first_step.how: Register through the Zoom registration link on the group's event page. Registration is required, so you get the meeting link after you sign up.
first_step.basis: Open to caregivers of neurodivergent children, with a clear registration link on the event page.
first_step.what_to_expect: Expect about an hour on Zoom with other caregivers of neurodivergent children, sharing experiences and what has worked. The listing does not say who facilitates or how many people attend.
first_visit_tips: Register ahead, since the meeting link comes after you sign up.
Log in a few minutes early to check your audio and video.
Ask the contact about facilitators or age limits, since the listing does not give them.

records.notes: This record id and its aka names cover more than one Healthy Minds group. The suicide loss group (Zoom, free, adults 18 and older, meets 2nd Wednesday 7 pm, 3rd Thursday 2 pm and 4th Tuesday 7 pm) is a different group and needs its own record; it is in leads_only. This record describes the caregiver group named on the record. The event page does not say the group repeats. Tier 1 saw listings for Oct 6, Nov 3 and Dec 1, 2026 (all Tuesdays), which supports monthly but is not stated on the page. Cost is not stated; tier 1 wrote free, and that is corrected to unknown. The phone number 267-507-3874 is carried over from tier 1 and does not appear on this event page; the 267-831-0333 dial-in belongs to the suicide loss group.

records.name: Swim Pony Performing Arts
records.summary: A Philadelphia theater company that makes immersive and playful devised shows, including interactive work in unusual spaces. Its site lists its shows but no current dates.
records.what_you_do: See one of the company's immersive shows when one is running, or support the company through its Can I Help page. The site lists no volunteer roles, classes or workshops.

schedule.text: Productions are one-off events, and the site shows no dates.

cost.text: Ticket prices are not shown on the site. Donations are taken through an online page run by the company's fiscal sponsor.

first_step.how: Use the contact form on the company's contact page to ask about the next show and tickets.
first_step.basis: Shows are open to the public, but the site lists no current dates, tickets or direct contact details, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The shows are immersive, playful devised pieces, and some are set in unusual places. The site does not say how long a show runs, where it is staged, or what it costs, so ask before you plan a visit.
first_visit_tips: Use the contact form to ask for the next show date and ticket details.
The site lists shows, not classes or workshops, so plan to see a show rather than take part.
The newest dated production on the site is from 2017, so confirm a show is running before you plan a trip.

records.notes: Status changed from probably_active to dormant. The newest dated items on the site are from 2017 (War of the Worlds, presented over Halloween weekend 2017 and described as a prototype) and the Cross Pollination seasons from 2014 to 2015 and 2015 to 2016. The other show pages show no dates. A web search for 2025 and 2026 news found no current listing. Kept as publish because the group is not shown to be closed, so the owner may want to hide it. The Philadelphia location comes from tier 1's Philadelphia Cultural Fund listing; the company's pages show no street address. One search snippet mentioned a 2020 app, but it had no confirmed source URL, so it was not used. Accessibility is not stated.

records.name: T21 Club of the Delaware Valley
records.summary: A club that supports awareness and inclusion for people born with Down syndrome in Pennsylvania, New Jersey and Delaware. It holds awareness events and runs fundraisers, such as a sock sale.
records.what_you_do: Take part in the club's awareness events, such as its Phillies event, or order Rock Your Socks to support its work.

cost.text: Dues and membership fees are not stated. Rock Your Socks costs $5 a pair for up to 20 pairs, $4 a pair for 21 to 99 pairs, and $3 a pair for over 100.

first_step.how: Email the club at T21clubofdelval@gmail.com or use its contact form to ask about the next awareness event and how to get involved.
first_step.basis: The site lists awareness events, a fundraiser and a contact form, but no meetings, volunteer roles or membership steps, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site describes awareness events and fundraisers, but not regular meetings. Ask the club what a visit to an event would look like before you go.
first_visit_tips: Ask which event is next and whether it is open to the public.
The site does not say the Grant Avenue address is a meeting place, so confirm before you go.

records.notes: The May 18, 2026 Phillies awareness event is the last sign of life; the Phillies page it links to was not read. The Rock Your Socks deadline of March 11 has no year on the page, so it is not used. The Grant Avenue address is listed, but the site does not say it is a meeting place. The site gives no meeting, volunteer, membership or dues information. Rock Your Socks orders go to a separate email address on the site, which is not recorded here. The contact name is carried over from tier 1 (IRS and NCCS records) and is not on the site. Accessibility is not stated.
